messages:
maria: heads up — we need to show SLO attribution in the console for embeddings requests broken down by routing policy and dim-bucket. product wants to know which routes trigger slow responses so they can decide on dedicated capacity.

aj: can you clarify what "SLO attribution" means here? is it per-tenant latency P95, or per-route, or per-shape? :thinking_face:

maria: per-route & per-shape. basically: when an embed request hits a variant route (small/medium/large dims) the console should show the SLO impact for that bucket and the routing policy that served it (primary, fallback, low-cost). want to correlate higher latency with fallback routing or oversize splitting.

sandeep: ok — we currently emit metrics with labels: `route`, `model_variant`, `latency_ms`, and `tenant_id`. we do NOT surface `dim_bucket` or `payload_slo_tag`. we can add labels but need to be careful about cardinality.

leo: cardinality is the big risk. we should derive a small finite set for `dim_bucket` (e.g., tiny|small|medium|large|oversize) and a `route_class` (primary|fallback|degraded). that's only 5x3 combos so fine.

maria: that sounds right. product also asked for a tie-in to quota buckets — i.e., which quota softcaps were hit that triggered splitting or fallback. we have `quota_reason` in some logs but it's freeform today. can we keep it enum-like?

aj: propose we standardize telemetry labels to: `dim_bucket`, `route_class`, `quota_flag` (none|softcap|hardcap), and `split_action` (none|prefetch|server_split). then map those to console SLO cards.

observability-bot: Note: adding new metric labels will increase cardinality by up to 45x when combined with existing `model_variant`. Recommend review with eng-infra before rollout.

leo: thanks bot. we can instead avoid emitting `model_variant` + `dim_bucket` together at high cardinality points. idea: emit a lightweight span with the full set for traces, and a compact metric which has a hashed `shape_class` label (tiny/small/...).

maria: can you sketch the runtime header that callers could set (optional) to help routing & telemetry? product prefers something client-side that helps attribution, but we also want defaults when clients don't send it.

sandeep: something like: `X-Embed-Shape: dims=1024;tokens=12` is too verbose. better: `X-Embed-Dim-Bucket: small` with an optional `X-Embed-Shape-Hint: dense|sparse`. sample payload ->
```
X-Embed-Dim-Bucket: medium
X-Embed-Shape-Hint: dense
X-Embed-Client: web-sdk-1.2.0
```

aj: love that. SDKs can compute the bucket with the same algorithm as the router so attribution is consistent. SDK sends header and routing also records the same bucket. If absent, router computes and sets `router.dim_bucket` label in telemetry.

maria: console UX ask: show a heatmap where X axis = dim_bucket, Y axis = route_class, cells show p50/p95 latency and percent of requests that required fallback/splits. also filter by tenant or model.

leo: implementation notes: console will need a mapping layer that consumes `dim_bucket` + `route_class` labels from metrics store. we'll expose a new per-route SLO card and a downloadable CSV. Might need a rolling 7d aggregation.

observability-bot: Heads-up: the metrics pipeline currently samples traces at 10% for embeddings. to get accurate split_action percents we should either increase sampling for requests with `split_action != none` or emit a metric counter `embed.split_action.count{dim_bucket,route_class,quota_flag}`.

sandeep: emitting counters is cheaper and lower-cardinality if we keep enums. I'll add `embed.split_action.count` and `embed.request.count` with the new labels. that solves percentages without trace sampling.

aj: UX/rollout plan: 1) runtime: add header parsing + router label; 2) metrics: add new counters and `dim_bucket` label; 3) console: new heatmap card behind a feature flag; 4) rollout + infra review. target: canary in staging next week.

maria: can we add an opt-in telemetry toggle at tenant level (for enterprise customers) since some may not want `dim_bucket` exported?

sandeep: yes — we'll honor tenant telemetry opt-out; router will still compute dim_bucket for routing but emit `dim_bucket=opted_out` as a label value in metrics to avoid leaking shape.

leo: small detail: what about embeddings with mixed dims in a single request? we should classify by max dim across items or `mixed` bucket. prefer `mixed` to avoid misattribution.

maria: agreed: bucket = max(dim) with the exception if items' dims vary > 3x -> bucket=mixed. Documenting that in the console tooltip will avoid confusion.

aj: I'll own the console feature flag and wireframes. sandeep — you own the metrics and header spec. leo — you own the router change and fallback enum. maria — you own stakeholder comms. I'll open a RFC PR with the header enum and an example dashboard JSON.

maria: perfect. @aj ping me when the RFC is up, I'll loop in product and sales for dedicated capacity recommendations. :+1:

observability-bot: Action created: METRICS-294 add `embed.split_action.count` and `embed.request.count` with labels `dim_bucket,route_class,quota_flag` — assigned to sandeep.

sandeep: noted. starting work today, will post a canary patch and example query for the console. :smile:

leo: FYI I'll add a small runtime doc snippet for the `X-Embed-Dim-Bucket` algorithm so SDKs match.

maria: thanks all — this should help product answer dedicated vs hosted cost/latency tradeoffs much faster. :rocket:
